comparator.name: Computational Social Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The regulations require five 30 EC modules and allow 30 EC of electives. Each required module builds on earlier work. The final capstone combines social research and data science to develop and implement a digital intervention with an external partner.

components.name: Foundation: Appreciating the complexity of social challenges
Building blocks: Experimenting with digital interventions for behavioural change
Connections: Linking data for better interventions in health or mobility systems
Structures: Applying responsible AI to reduce inequality
Electives, minor, internship or study abroad
Capstone: Making social change with digital innovations

courseTraceability.rationale: Econometrics Uses regression, instrumental variables and simulation to distinguish causal questions from prediction in an empirical paper.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Computational social science combining human behaviour, social research and data-driven public problem solving” and “Programming, data analysis, visualisation and machine learning for social impact”.

basisLabels: Project-based digital intervention, stakeholder collaboration and responsible innovation
How can data and digital interventions improve climate, mobility or health systems?
courseTraceability.rationale: Public Policy Analysis Analyses policy development across jurisdictions and communicates findings through policy memos.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Project-based digital intervention, stakeholder collaboration and responsible innovation” and “How can data and digital interventions improve climate, mobility or health systems?”.

basisLabels: Responsible AI, inequality, surveillance and algorithmic power
How do surveillance, algorithms and AI reproduce or reduce social inequality?
courseTraceability.rationale: Social Movements & Environmental Justice Compares environmental justice movements and forms of collective action as a concrete domain for examining unequal impacts and responses.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Responsible AI, inequality, surveillance and algorithmic power” and “How do surveillance, algorithms and AI reproduce or reduce social inequality?”.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad option brings computation, behavioural research and public problem solving together. The climate option emphasises spatial data and environmental policy. The responsible AI option emphasises models, inequality and digital power. The three distinct options reach the maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both teach data preparation and visualisation. UCR uses R in a dedicated data science course, while UvA combines these skills with Python and social research projects.
Both build and evaluate predictive models. UvA combines modelling with stakeholder engagement and analysis of algorithmic bias.
Both analyse stakeholders and develop policy responses to complex systems. UCR focuses on sustainability governance. UvA develops an intervention plan for a health or mobility system.
Both involve team research on a problem from an external partner. UCR investigates a regional sustainability question. UvA also implements a digital intervention in its final semester.
Both use design thinking and prototyping. UCR tests a venture idea, while UvA tests a digital intervention for behaviour change.
The fifth semester offers 30 EC of elective study, a minor, an approved internship or study abroad.

notes.text: UvA teaches social research, computation and intervention design together in semester-long projects. UCR develops related skills across separate courses. The required UvA capstone includes implementing a digital intervention for an external partner.
UvA reserves the fifth semester for 30 EC of electives, a minor, an approved internship or study abroad.

audience.programmeDescription: Computational Social Science at the University of Amsterdam combines social research and computing to investigate public problems and develop digital interventions. Students work on projects about climate, surveillance, health or mobility, and inequality.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines social research, computing and public problem solving. The other options concentrate on spatial data and environmental policy, or on responsible AI and inequality.

componentNotes.y1-building: Students design and pilot a digital intervention for behaviour change.
componentNotes.y2-connections: Students prepare a plan for an intervention in a health or mobility system.
componentNotes.y2-structures: Students build a predictive model and examine risks of algorithmic bias.
componentNotes.y3-capstone: Teams submit a research report and implement a digital intervention with an external partner.
